articles.title: Ryan Gosling’s Zero-G Stunts on ‘Project Hail Mary’ Broken Down by the Space Epic’s VFX Supervisors
articles.summary: For Oscar-winning VFX supervisor Paul Lambert Lambert, of all the huge challenges presented by Ryan Gosling space epic “Project Hail Mary,” the most daunting was creating convincing zero gravity.
body: “Zero-G was probably my personal biggest concern going into the movie,” he said at View Conference in Turin, Italy, drilling down on its VFX.

Other experiments were deliberately hands-on. Fraser used an infrared-modified camera, programmable IR lights and water running in front of the lens to develop some of the film’s stranger imagery. “It was literally a mad science lab,” Lambert recalled. Burning fireballs, liquids, lasers and ferrofluid were also filmed to provide starting points for the microscopic effects.

The DP returned during postproduction to work with ILM’s Helios virtual-camera system on the sequence near Adrian. Artists tracked Gosling’s on-set performance and recreated it within digital environments, allowing Fraser to choose new camera positions without discarding the original acting.

Across those techniques, the supervisors’ ambition remained consistent: to make even the most elaborate effects obey a recognizable physical logic while ensuring Rocky felt as present beside Gosling as any human scene partner.

articles.summary: Quentin Tarantino has long said he’ll be retiring after his tenth feature film, but fans shouldn’t worry yet. While the “Pulp Fiction” director confirmed he’d finished penning the script for his final project, he won’t be getting much further with it until his newly opened play, “The Popinjay…
body: He also gave audiences more insight into “The Popinjay Cavalier,” which he said started as a screenplay before the director realized “it really worked as a play.” “I think it will be thrilling,” he said.

Starring Sacha Baron Cohen, “The Popinjay Cavalier” will open at London’s Phoenix Theatre next March, following previews in late Feb. The play, described as a “swashbuckling comedy,” is set to run for three months, closing on June 13. “I’m keen with anticipation to give the West End a great night out,” Tarantino said in a statement when the show was announced.

Tarantino’s most recent release remains “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood,” which came out in 2019 and starred Brad Pitt, Leonardo DiCaprio, Margot Robbie, Margaret Qualley and more. Pitt won the Oscar for best supporting actor that year, as did Barbara Ling and Nancy Haigh for best production design. Tarantino was also nominated for best picture and best director, while DiCaprio was nominated for best actor.

articles.title: James McAvoy Says ‘Split’ Is The Only Film That ‘Really Consistently Pays Me’
articles.summary: James McAvoy has starred in films including “Speak No Evil,” “Atonement” and “X-Men: First Class,” but he recently revealed the “only” film he still consistently receives residuals from is M.
body: In “Split,” three girls are kidnapped by a man with a diagnosed 23 distinct personalities (McAvoy). “They must try to escape before the apparent emergence of a frightful new 24th,” per the film’s official description. Anya Taylor-Joy, Haley Lu Richardson and Jessica Sula starred alongside McAvoy. The film, which cost just $6 million to make, went on to gross $138.29 million domestically and $140.16 million internationally for a $278.45 million worldwide total.
McAvoy also spoke about Shyamalan and his experience working with the director.

“I very consciously took from many of the directors that I worked with, and subconsciously as well, but the thing I took away from him is his preparedness,” McAvoy said. “He made that film, and [sequel] ‘Glass,’ on incredibly modest budgets, and very focused on how he would maximize his day and maximize his shots and maximize what he got out of the story by just being incredibly well-prepared and being able to share that and communicate that with the crew.”

articles.title: 7 Miles Out review – Carol Morley’s funny-poignant self-portrait of teenage kicks in Stockport
articles.summary: A daring, rich and funny study of the ordeal of having to invent and reinvent your own teenage sense of self amid confounding changes. Carol Morley’s self-portrait of the artist as a young woman is rich, tender and terribly funny and sad: a study in the chaos of being young and a triptych of…
body: 7 Miles Out is based on Morley’s autobiographical novel of the same title, the once-upon-a-time-in-Stockport story of Ann, played with charm and zing by Lucy Halliday, and as a sweetly innocent young girl by Amelie Hughes. Young Ann pretends to be making a radio programme with her cassette recorder the way so many did in the 1970s, and hero-worships her would-be rock journalist elder brother Scott (Kasper Hilton-Hille) – based on Morley’s brother Paul – who is already plugged into the burgeoning post-punk and new wave scene.

Ann’s mum Bryn, wonderfully played by Gemma Whelan, is capable and good-humoured in a no-nonsense sort of way, but later to be beset with anger and mercurial depression. She has however found something to smile about now in the news that her husband and Ann’s dad Ronald, played by Aidan Gillen, has found a prestigious new job in Manchester – seven miles out. So to get to work, he has apparently been supplied with a handsome, though not brand-new car.
points: A daring, rich and funny study of the ordeal of having to invent and reinvent your own teenage sense of self amid confounding changes.

articles.title: South Africa’s Oscar Entry ‘Variations on a Theme’ Was Written With Microsoft Excel
articles.summary: Plus, an Estonian composer also has something to do with the film’s musical vibes, co-writer and co-director Devon Delmar shared with THR at the BFI London Film Festival.
body: Ouma Hettie is an octogenarian goat herder in South Africa’s Kamiesberge. When she falls victim to a scam promising reparation for her father’s unpaid service during World War II, her family becomes more involved than she would like them to.
“A poetic and distinctive visual style infuses playfulness into this insightful study of a woman’s resilience and a community that exists close to the land,” the LFF website said about the film.
Delmar, who also edited the film, came to London for LFF snd talked to THR about the musicalness of Variations on a Theme and how it may well be the only movie ever to be written on Microsoft Excel.
The film has a rhythmic dance vibe, a sense of an underlying choreography that you just feel while experiencing it – without necessarily being able to explain that feeling. And that is all by design.

articles.title: How The Traitors' music plays with your emotions
articles.summary: It's not just treachery and villainy - the soundtrack for Traitors helps set the show's campy tone.
body: Have you ever noticed how the soundtrack manipulates your perception? A sinister orchestral flourish hints at a double cross. A cheeky chord injects humour into a kitchen conflab.
As ever, though, you shouldn't trust what happens in the castle. The music can provide emphasis or act as misdirection, all at the producers' behest.

"I remember the BBC was quite reluctant to even think about a show with murder as a main feature, so I knew I didn't want the music to go really dark," says Sam Watts, who composed the opening theme and much of the incidental score (but is not responsible for the show's haunting cover versions of well-known pop songs... more on those later).

Watts, who had previously worked on Planet Earth and The Sarah Jane Adventures, pitched to work on the programme with only a basic idea of the set-up. It was only when he learned Winkleman was the host that he settled on his approach.

articles.title: Busan 2026: Zogsool, Full Moon, Beyond Love’s Horizon
articles.summary: My final dispatch from Busan features what might be the most eclectic titles at the festival. They all hail from the Vision section. The first is in the Asia vertical while the final two are in the Korean.
body: Set at the outset of the COVID-19 pandemic in Mongolia, “ Zogsool,” which means “The Station,” is a dark, thorny politically fraught romantic comedy that finds truth in its broad visual approach.

Written and directed by Byamba Sakhya, the film follows Khanda (Bulgan Chuluunbat), a flinty single mother who manages a far-flung petrol station as she raises her teenage daughter. In this small provincial village, Khanda almost welcomes conflict. For one, everyone is in debt to her because they’ve borrowed gas on credit. One shaggy scoundrel even tries to pay her with a sheep, an offer she bitterly refuses. Khanda also ridicules an experienced coach who wants to enlist her daughter in a martial arts competition happening in the city and understandably openly recoils at her boss (Tumurbaatar Tsegmid), who coaxes her to sexually please him.
points: My final dispatch from Busan features what might be the most eclectic titles at the festival.
The first is in the Asia vertical while the final two are in the Korean.

articles.title: Selma Blair ‘did not intend to harm anyone’ during airplane incident, representatives say
articles.summary: Actor experienced a ‘medical emergency’ on flight during which she allegedly injured crew members, statement says. Actor Selma Blair did not mean to hurt anyone during the recent flight which led to her arrest on allegations that she assaulted a pair of cabin crew members, a police officer and a…
body: The lengthy statement also dismissed prior media coverage of Blair’s arrest after a Delta Air Lines flight from Los Angeles to New York as unsympathetic and inaccurate, singling out reporting from several outlets alleging that she tried to open the door of the airplane that she and her fellow passengers were on.
“Selma Blair experienced a medical emergency on the flight,” her representatives’ statement contended. “There was no attempt to open the door of the aircraft. Selma did not intend to harm anyone.”

Friday’s statement from Blair’s camp added some contours to brief remarks made in the days since her arrest by her publicist and lawyer which maintained that there had been a medical emergency but did not elaborate much.

Without specifying who may have done so, the statement on Friday called it “outrageous” for anyone to suggest Blair does not have multiple sclerosis (MS), a chronic neurological disorder which she went public about being diagnosed with in 2018.

articles.title: Manifest: From reality TV to Wembley Arena in one turbulent year
articles.summary: Turkish girl group manifest on taking their music to a global audience, as they prepare for their first UK concert.
body: When I first meet Turkish girl group manifest, we're on a boat cruising down the River Thames.
The six band members are clutching Union jack umbrellas as they pose for press photographs and mingle with British pop acts, including K-pop-trained boyband dearALICE.
Netflix cameras are filming the evening for a six-part documentary. The group are in London hoping to build on their success in Turkey and reach an international audience.
Their ambitions come after a turbulent year at home, during which the band were prosecuted for public indecency over their outfits and dance moves during a concert in Istanbul.
